newsitem.title: USA: Gillette says U.S. dollar hurt sales gains.
newsitem.headline: Gillette says U.S. dollar hurt sales gains.

text.p: Gillette Co said Thursday that the strong U.S. dollar cut into its sales gains in the first quarter by three percentage points and that it experienced soft economic conditions in some key markets.
In the quarter, the company reported sales of $2.18 billion, a gain of 6 percent from $2.06 billion in the same period in the prior year.
Gillette, the maker of razors, toiletries, cosmetics and stationary products, said net income rose to $283.7 million, or $0.51 per share, from $249.3 million, or $0.45 per share.

The company said in a statement that blade and razor sales during the period were "moderately higher." Sales and profits in its Duracell division were "substantially higher" than the prior year, it said.
First quarter sales of Braun products were slightly lower than in the comparable period a year ago, while profits were down moderately, it said.
Toiletries and cosmetics sales for the first quarter rose considerably, while profits grew substantially, the company said.
Sales of stationery products in the first quarter declined "well below" the prior year's, while profits were virtually unchanged, it said.
Oral-B sales and profits for the first quarter "strongly surpassed" those of last year.
The company did not provide dollar amounts for each division. A spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
A company spokesman later in the day provided the following breakdown of sales and operating profits:
First quarter blade and razor sales were up four percent to $615.1 million versus $594.1 million. Its operating profit was up 12 percent to $264.7 million from $236.1 million.
Sales in its toiletries and cosmetics segment were up nine percent to $309.2 million from $282.9 million. Operating profit in that segment grew 75 percent to $32.3 million from $18.5 million.
Stationery product sales dropped eight percent to $189.6 million from $206 million. Operating profit in that segment was essentially flat at $26.8 million from $26.9 million.
Braun sales dropped three percent to $465.9 million from $479.2 million, while its operating profit shrunk four percent to $89.9 million from $93.2 million.
Oral-B sales jumped 16 percent to $133.3 million from $114.6 million, while its operating profits grew 11 percent to $12.2 million from $11 million.
Sales in its Duracell batteries segment grew 22 percent to $467.4 million from $382 million, while operating profits increased 24 percent to $53.8 million from $43.5 million.
